boss.briefing: Hess's law: knock out the power couplings one step at a time
boss.context:
Find ΔH for  C(graphite) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g)
(1)  C(graphite) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g)      ΔH = −393.5 kJ
(2)  CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g)      ΔH = −283.0 kJ

questions.prompt: A hot drink sealed in a perfectly insulated thermos can exchange neither matter nor energy with its surroundings. What kind of system is it?
questions.explanation: An isolated system exchanges neither matter nor energy. A closed system exchanges energy only, and an open system exchanges both.

questions.prompt: An uncovered beaker of water boils on a hot plate. What kind of system is the water?
choices: None, because it is the surroundings
questions.explanation: Water vapor (matter) escapes and heat (energy) flows in, so matter and energy are both exchanged. That makes it an open system.

questions.prompt: A stoppered flask of gas is warmed in a water bath. What kind of system is the gas?
questions.explanation: The stopper keeps matter in, but heat still passes through the glass. Energy without matter means a closed system.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a state function?
questions.explanation: State functions depend only on the initial and final states. Heat (q) and work (w) depend on the path taken, so they are not state functions.

questions.prompt: An ice cube melts on a countertop. Describe the process, taking the ice as the system.
choices: Endothermic: heat flows from the surroundings into the system
Exothermic: heat flows from the system into the surroundings
Endothermic: heat flows from the system into the surroundings
Exothermic: heat flows from the surroundings into the system
questions.explanation: Melting absorbs heat. Energy flows from the surroundings into the ice, so the process is endothermic (q > 0).

questions.prompt: A reaction flask becomes hot to the touch. Which statement is correct?
choices: The reaction is exothermic; heat flows from the system to the surroundings
The reaction is endothermic; heat flows from the surroundings to the system
The reaction is exothermic; heat flows from the surroundings to the system
No heat is transferred; only the temperature changes
questions.explanation: Your hand is part of the surroundings. It warms up because the reaction (the system) releases heat, so the reaction is exothermic (q < 0).

questions.prompt: Energy stored in the chemical bonds of fuel is best described as…
choices: Chemical energy, a form of potential energy
Thermal energy, a form of kinetic energy
Kinetic energy of the fuel molecules
questions.explanation: Chemical energy is potential energy stored in the arrangement of atoms and electrons in bonds. Combustion releases it.

questions.prompt: One calorie (cal) is equal to…
questions.explanation: 1 cal = 4.184 J exactly. A food Calorie (capital C) is 1 kcal = 4184 J.

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs {q} J of heat and does {w} J of work on its surroundings. What is ΔU of the gas?
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed means q = +{q} J. Work done BY the gas means w = −{w} J. So ΔU = q + w = {ans}.

questions.prompt: A system releases {q} J of heat while the surroundings do {w} J of work on it. What is ΔU?
questions.explanation: Heat released means q = −{q} J. Work done ON the system means w = +{w} J. So ΔU = q + w = {ans}.

questions.prompt: Under the sign conventions in this course, work done BY a system on its surroundings is…
questions.explanation: Energy that leaves the system is negative. A system that does work loses energy, so w < 0. Work done ON the system is positive.

questions.prompt: A gas expands from {v1} L to {v2} L against a constant external pressure of {p} atm. Calculate w in joules.  (1 L·atm = 101.3 J)
questions.explanation: w = −PΔV = −({p} atm)({v2} − {v1} L) × 101.3 J/(L·atm) = {ans}. Expansion work done by the gas is negative.

questions.prompt: For a process, q = +250 J and w = −250 J. What is ΔU?
questions.explanation: ΔU = q + w = (+250 J) + (−250 J) = 0 J. The heat absorbed exactly balances the work done by the system.

questions.prompt: Internal energy is a state function. What does ΔU depend on?
choices: Only the initial and final states
The path taken between the states
questions.explanation: Any path between the same two states gives the same ΔU, even though q and w can each differ from path to path.

questions.prompt:
CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)    ΔH = −890.4 kJ/mol
How much heat is released when {g} g of CH₄ burns?  (CH₄ = 16.04 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles of CH₄ = {g} g ÷ 16.04 g/mol. Each mole releases 890.4 kJ, so heat released = {ans}.

questions.prompt:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g)    ΔH = −92.2 kJ
What is ΔH for  2NH₃(g) → N₂(g) + 3H₂(g)?
questions.explanation: Reversing a thermochemical equation changes the sign of ΔH but not its size: −92.2 kJ becomes +92.2 kJ.

questions.prompt:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g)    ΔH = −92.2 kJ
What is ΔH for  ½N₂(g) + 3/2 H₂(g) → NH₃(g)?
questions.explanation: Multiplying an equation by a factor multiplies ΔH by the same factor: ½ × (−92.2 kJ) = −46.1 kJ.

questions.prompt: At constant pressure, the enthalpy change ΔH equals…
choices: The heat absorbed or released, q (at constant P)
The work done by the system
The temperature change times the mass
questions.explanation: ΔH = qₚ. The enthalpy change is the heat transferred at constant pressure, which is how most bench reactions run.

questions.prompt: A reaction has ΔH = +58 kJ. Which statement is true?
choices: It is endothermic; it absorbs heat from the surroundings
It is exothermic; it releases heat to the surroundings
It is endothermic; it releases heat to the surroundings
questions.explanation: A positive ΔH means the products have more enthalpy than the reactants, so heat is absorbed: the reaction is endothermic.

questions.prompt:
2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l)    ΔH = −571.6 kJ
What is ΔH when {n} mol of H₂O(l) is formed?
questions.explanation: The equation shows −571.6 kJ per 2 mol of H₂O, which is −285.8 kJ per mol. Multiply by {n} mol: ΔH = {ans}.

questions.prompt: How much heat is needed to warm {m} g of water from {t1} °C to {t2} °C?  (s = 4.184 J/g·°C)
A {m} g piece of iron (s = 0.444 J/g·°C) absorbs {q} J of heat. By how much does its temperature rise?
A reaction runs in a coffee-cup calorimeter and the solution warms up. Which relationship applies?
questions.explanation: The heat released by the reaction (system) is absorbed by the solution (surroundings): q(sys) = −q(surr). The solution warms, so q(rxn) < 0.

questions.prompt: {v} mL of 1.0 M HCl and {v} mL of 1.0 M NaOH, both at {t1} °C, are mixed in a coffee-cup calorimeter. The temperature rises to {t2} °C. Taking the solution as {ms} g with s = 4.184 J/g·°C, what is q(rxn)?
questions.explanation: q(soln) = smΔT = (4.184)({ms} g)({t2} − {t1} °C) in J. The reaction released that heat, so q(rxn) = −q(soln) = {ans}.

questions.prompt: A sample burns in a constant-volume bomb calorimeter whose heat capacity is C(cal) = {c} kJ/°C. The temperature rises by {dt} °C. What is q(rxn)?
questions.explanation: q(cal) = C(cal)·ΔT = ({c} kJ/°C)({dt} °C). The calorimeter absorbs the heat the reaction releases: q(rxn) = −C(cal)ΔT = {ans}.

questions.prompt: Which quantity has units of J/°C?
questions.explanation: Heat capacity C = ms is for a whole object (J/°C). Specific heat s is per gram (J/g·°C), and molar heat capacity is per mole (J/mol·°C).

questions.prompt: Equal masses of water (s = 4.184 J/g·°C) and copper (s = 0.385 J/g·°C) absorb the same amount of heat. Which one warms up more?
choices: Copper, because its specific heat is lower
Water, because its specific heat is higher
They warm by the same amount
questions.explanation: ΔT = q / (sm). With q and m the same, the smaller s gives the larger ΔT. Copper's temperature rises about 11 times as much.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents the standard enthalpy of formation of CO₂(g)?
questions.explanation: ΔH°f forms exactly 1 mol of the compound from its elements in their standard states. Carbon's standard state is graphite, not diamond.

questions.prompt: For which substance is ΔH°f equal to zero?
questions.explanation: ΔH°f = 0 for an element in its most stable form at 1 atm and 25 °C. That is O₂(g), not ozone, and graphite, not diamond.

questions.prompt:
Find ΔH°rxn for  CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
ΔH°f (kJ/mol): CH₄(g) −74.85, CO₂(g) −393.5, H₂O(l) −285.8
questions.explanation: ΔH°rxn = ΣnΔH°f(products) − ΣmΔH°f(reactants) = [−393.5 + 2(−285.8)] − [−74.85 + 2(0)] = −890.3 kJ.

questions.prompt:
Find ΔH°rxn for  2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g)
ΔH°f (kJ/mol): H₂O₂(l) −187.6, H₂O(l) −285.8
questions.explanation: ΔH°rxn = [2(−285.8) + 0] − [2(−187.6)] = −571.6 + 375.2 = −196.4 kJ. O₂(g) is an element in its standard state, so its ΔH°f is 0.

questions.prompt: For the reaction  2A + B → C,  ΔH°f(A) = {a}, ΔH°f(B) = {b} and ΔH°f(C) = {c} kJ/mol. What is ΔH°rxn?
questions.explanation: ΔH°rxn = ΣnΔH°f(products) − ΣmΔH°f(reactants) = ({c}) − [2({a}) + ({b})] = {ans}. Remember to multiply each ΔH°f by its coefficient.

questions.prompt: The standard state for tabulated ΔH°f values refers to…
choices: 1 atm pressure, usually at 25 °C, with each element in its most stable form
Any temperature, provided the pressure is 1 atm
The gas phase for every substance
questions.explanation: Standard enthalpies of formation are tabulated at 1 atm and 25 °C (298 K), with each element in its most stable form.

questions.prompt: STEP 1: CO(g) has to end up as a product. What must you do to equation (2)?
choices: Reverse it, so ΔH becomes +283.0 kJ
Reverse it and keep ΔH = −283.0 kJ
Multiply it by 2, so ΔH becomes −566.0 kJ
questions.explanation: CO is a reactant in (2) but a product in the target, so reverse (2). Reversing an equation flips the sign of ΔH: +283.0 kJ.

questions.prompt: STEP 2: Add equation (1) to the reversed equation (2). Which species cancel?
choices: CO₂(g), and ½O₂(g) from the O₂ on the left
questions.explanation: C + O₂ + CO₂ → CO₂ + CO + ½O₂. CO₂ cancels from both sides, and ½O₂ cancels, leaving ½O₂ on the left: C + ½O₂ → CO.

questions.prompt: STEP 3: What is ΔH for  C(graphite) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g)?
questions.explanation: Hess's law: add the ΔH values of the equations you added. ΔH = −393.5 kJ + 283.0 kJ = −110.5 kJ.
